working: R2 -> R2-R1 gives (2a\lambda+\lambda^2,...); R3 -> R3-R1 gives (-2a\lambda+\lambda^2,...). Then R2 -> R2+R3 = 2\lambda^2(1,1,1) and R3 -> R3-\frac12 R2 = -2\lambda(a,b,c), so D = 2\lambda^2 \cdot (-2\lambda) \cdot \det[a^2,b^2,c^2;1,1,1;a,b,c] = 4\lambda^3 \det[a^2,b^2,c^2;a,b,c;1,1,1] after swapping the last two rows. working: S is not reflexive: (x,x) in S would need x = x+1, impossible, so S is not an equivalence relation. T: x-x = 0 is an integer (reflexive); x-y integer implies y-x integer (symmetric); x-y and y-z integers imply x-z integer (transitive), so T is an equivalence relation.

working: Replacing x by 1/x gives f(1/x) + 2f(x) = 3/x. Doubling this and subtracting the original: 3f(x) = 6/x - 3x, so f(x) = 2/x - x. Then f(x) = f(-x) gives 2/x - x = -2/x + x, i.e. 4/x = 2x, x^2 = 2, x = \pm\sqrt{2} — exactly two elements. Check: f(\sqrt2) = 2/\sqrt2 - \sqrt2 = 0 = f(-\sqrt2).

f'(x) = 6x^2 - 30x + 36 = 6(x-2)(x-3), so f increases on [0,2) and decreases on (2,3] — not one-one (e.g. f(1) = 24 and f(2.?) repeats values in [28,29]). f(0)=1, f(2)=29, f(3)=28, so the image is [1,29] exactly, hence onto. Onto but not one-one.

working: Rows 1 and 2 of A are e_1, e_2 so they are unchanged in A^2. Row 3 of A^2 = a(1,0,0) + b(0,1,0) + (-1)(a,b,-1) = (0,0,1). Hence A^2 = I, the unit matrix (A is an involutory matrix).
Symmetric gives A^T = A and skew-symmetric gives A^T = -A, so A = -A, i.e. 2A = 0 and A = O, the null matrix.

working: From 1+\omega+\omega^2 = 0 we get 1+\omega = -\omega^2, so 1+\omega-\omega^2 = -\omega^2 - \omega^2 = -2\omega^2. Then (-2\omega^2)^7 = -128\,\omega^{14} = -128\,\omega^{2} since 14 \equiv 2 \pmod 3.
(1+i)/(1-i) = (1+i)^2/((1-i)(1+i)) = 2i/2 = i. So i^x = 1, which holds exactly when x is a multiple of 4, i.e. x = 4n.

z^2+z+1=0 makes z a primitive cube root of unity, so z^3 = 1 and 1/z = z^2. Then z+1/z = z+z^2 = -1; z^2+1/z^2 = z^2+z = -1; z^3+1/z^3 = 1+1 = 2; and the pattern repeats with period 3. Squares: 1, 1, 4, 1, 1, 4 summing to 12.
a = ar + ar^2 with a > 0 gives r^2 + r - 1 = 0, so r = (-1 \pm \sqrt5)/2. Terms are positive so r > 0, giving r = (\sqrt5-1)/2 \approx 0.618. Check: 0.618 + 0.618^2 = 0.618 + 0.382 = 1.

AP gives 2y = x+z. The arctan AP gives 2\tan^{-1}y = \tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}z, i.e. 2y/(1-y^2) = (x+z)/(1-xz) = 2y/(1-xz), so for y \neq 0 we get y^2 = xz. Thus x,y,z are simultaneously in AP and GP, which forces x = y = z.
notes: Edge case worth flagging for the reviewer (not source damage): if y = 0 the step dividing by 2y is invalid, and x = -1, y = 0, z = 1 satisfies both stated AP conditions (-1,0,1 in AP; -\pi/4, 0, \pi/4 in AP) without x = y = z. So (D) is the intended answer but is not strictly forced; the other three options are each disprovable, so (D) is still the only defensible choice.
